method_card.title: TV, Film and Streaming
method_card.content:
This lesson covers vocabulary for TV programmes, film genres and streaming habits, opinion phrases, and the perfect tense for talking about what you have watched.

GermanEnglish
das Fernsehentelevision
fernsehen (separable)to watch TV
die Sendung / das Programmprogramme
die Serieseries
der Filmfilm
der Dokumentarfilmdocumentary
die Komödiecomedy
der Krimicrime film / detective series
der Actionfilmaction film
der Zeichentrickfilmanimated film / cartoon
das Streaming / streamenstreaming / to stream
die Nachrichten (pl.)the news
spannendexciting / gripping
lustig / witzigfunny
langweiligboring
ich finde es...I find it... / I think it is...

Grammar focus — Perfect tense: Use haben + past participle at the end of the clause to say what you watched. Sehen is an irregular strong verb: past participle = gesehen. Example: Ich habe gestern einen spannenden Film gesehen. (I watched an exciting film yesterday.) The past participle sits at the very end; the auxiliary habe is at position 2. In a subordinate clause: weil ich einen Film gesehen habe — both verbs go to the end, conjugated verb last.

Note on fernsehen: This is a separable verb. In a main clause the prefix splits off: Ich sehe jeden Abend fern. (I watch TV every evening.) In a subordinate clause it stays whole at the end: weil ich jeden Abend fernsehe.

Model paragraph: Ich sehe am liebsten Krimiserien, weil sie spannend sind. Letzte Woche habe ich einen lustigen Zeichentrickfilm gestreamt. Ich finde es toll, weil man viele Serien online streamen kann. (I like watching crime series most of all because they are gripping. Last week I streamed a funny animated film. I think it's great because you can stream lots of series online.)
steps: Learn the TV and film genre vocabulary including each noun's gender (der/die/das)
Master the perfect tense for past viewing: haben + past participle at the clause end
Practise opinion phrases with weil clauses — remember the verb goes to the end after weil
Use fernsehen as a separable verb: Ich sehe fern (main clause) vs weil ich fernsehe (subordinate)
Build full sentences combining genre vocab and tenses with correctly capitalised nouns

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — TV and film appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate into English: 'Ich habe letzte Woche einen lustigen Actionfilm gesehen.'

steps.label: Identify the tense
steps.content: habe ... gesehen = perfect tense of sehen (to see/watch). The auxiliary habe is at position 2; the past participle gesehen is at the end.

steps.label: Spot the adjective ending
steps.content: einen lustigen Actionfilm — the adjective lustig has the ending -en because Film is masculine and follows einen (masculine accusative).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Last week I watched a funny action film.

worked_examples.question: Translate into German: 'I like watching crime series because they are exciting.'

steps.label: Choose the right verb for liking
steps.content: 'I like watching' = Ich sehe gern (using the adverb gern). Alternatively Ich sehe am liebsten (I like ... most of all). Both are correct.

steps.label: Add the weil clause
steps.content: After weil, the conjugated verb goes to the end: weil sie spannend sind — NOT weil sie sind spannend.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich sehe gern Krimiserien, weil sie spannend sind.

bronze.question: Match the German to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct adjective ending

gaps.rule: Adjective ending — masculine accusative after einen
gaps.correct_explain: After einen (masculine accusative), the adjective takes the ending -en: einen spannenden Film.

wrong.er: -er is the masculine nominative ending after ein. Here it is the direct object (accusative) of gesehen, so use -en.
wrong.e: -e is the feminine nominative ending. Film is masculine → -en in the accusative.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct word
sentence_parts: es toll, weil die Serie sehr spannend ist.

gaps.correct_explain: finde is the ich form of finden (to find/think). Ich finde es toll = I think it's great.

wrong.finden: finden is the infinitive or wir/sie form. The subject here is ich → finde.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich sehe am liebsten Krimiserien, weil sie spannend sind' mean?
options: I like watching crime series most of all because they are exciting
I don't like watching crime series because they are boring
I watched a crime series yesterday because it was exciting
I like watching crime series although they are sometimes scary

bronze.question: What does 'Meiner Meinung nach ist der neue Film langweilig' mean?
options: In my opinion the new film is boring
I think the new film is exciting
My friend says the new film is boring
The new film was boring last night

bronze.source_text: Mein Lieblingsfilm ist eine Komödie, die sehr witzig ist.
model_answers: My favourite film is a comedy that is very funny.

silver.question: Complete the sentence — type the missing words
silver.english: I **watched** an exciting series and I **found** it really good.
sentence_parts: und ich habe sie wirklich gut

gaps.correct_explain: gesehen is the irregular past participle of sehen (to see/watch). It goes at the end of the clause.

wrong.geseht: geseht is not a valid form. Sehen is irregular: the past participle is gesehen.
wrong.gesieht: gesieht does not exist. The past participle of sehen is gesehen.

gaps.correct_explain: gefunden is the irregular past participle of finden (to find). It goes at the end of the clause.

wrong.gefindet: gefindet is not a word. Finden is irregular: past participle = gefunden.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ein spannender Film ist mein Lieblingsfilm, aber ich habe eine langweilige Serie gesieht.
silver.explanation: Sehen is a strong (irregular) verb. Its past participle is gesehen, not gesieht. Strong verbs change their stem vowel: sehen → gesehen.
silver.translation: An exciting film is my favourite film, but I watched a boring series.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: In my opinion the new series is very exciting.

distractor_labels.neuer: wrong adjective ending — after die (definite article, feminine nominative), the adjective takes -e: die neue Serie, not die neuer Serie

silver.source_text: I like watching documentaries because they are interesting.
model_answers: Ich sehe gern Dokumentarfilme, weil sie interessant sind.

model_answers: Letzte Woche habe ich einen langweiligen Horrorfilm gesehen, aber ich würde sagen, dass die neue Komödie viel besser ist, weil sie wirklich lustig ist.

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I would say that the new series is disappointing.

distractor_labels.den: wrong — Serie is feminine, so the article is die (not den, which is masculine accusative)
distractor_labels.sagt: wrong verb form — sagt is present tense er/sie/es; here we need würde + infinitive sagen for the conditional
distractor_labels.neues: wrong adjective ending — neues is neuter; Serie is feminine (die Serie) → neue

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a cinema box office in Germany. You want to buy tickets and find out about the film showing tonight.

bullets.prompt: Greet the member of staff and ask for two tickets for the film this evening.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Ich möchte bitte zwei Karten für den Film heute Abend.
bullets.note: Guten Tag (formal greeting) + ich möchte + accusative zwei Karten + heute Abend (time phrase)

bullets.prompt: Ask what type of film it is and how long it lasts.
bullets.model_answer: Was für ein Film ist das? Wie lange dauert er?
bullets.note: Was für ein Film...? (what type of film?) + Wie lange dauert er? (How long does it last?)

bullets.prompt: Say you watched a comedy last week and it was very funny.
bullets.model_answer: Letzte Woche habe ich eine Komödie gesehen und sie war sehr witzig.
bullets.note: Perfect tense: habe + gesehen at end; letzte Woche (time adverb, verb stays at position 2); war (simple past of sein for description)

bullets.prompt: Say you will come back tomorrow if the film is good.
bullets.model_answer: Wenn der Film gut ist, werde ich morgen wiederkommen.
bullets.note: wenn + verb-final (ist at end of wenn clause); werden + infinitive for future; inversion after wenn clause (werde ich)

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error (Higher: adjective endings)
gold.sentence: Ich habe einen spannender Dokumentarfilm gesehen.
gold.explanation: After einen (masculine accusative indefinite article), the adjective ending is -en, not -er (which is the masculine nominative ending after ein). Correct: einen spannenden Dokumentarfilm.
